title: Plank theorems, Gaussian probabilistic estimates and Rump's 100 Euro conjecture
summary: We prove Rump's 100-euro conjecture by deriving a weighted affine escape theorem from Ball's plank theorem in [Invent. Math. \textbf{104} (1991)]. More precisely, let $\mathbb{K}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}$ and let $A\in\mathbb{K}^{n\times n}$. For every $1\le p\le \infty$, we obtain an $\ell_p$-escape principle controlled by the row $\ell_q$-norms of $A$. Its cube case shows that $|A|e=ne$, where $e$ is the all-one vector, implies the existence of a nonzero vector $x$ satisfying $\|x\|_{\infty}\le 1$ and $|Ax|\ge e\ge |x|$, thereby settling the conjecture.
